summary: Mikisaburo Mori was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932). He held academic posts at Osaka University (~1950–1973) and Bukkyo University (~1973–1980).

Ming Mei specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London with Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (BA 1966–1974) and earned a PhD at UCLA (1974–1979) under Kenneth Kuan Sheng Ch'en and Robert C. Epp, later serving as Professor at HKU (~1982–2012).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Shi Huifeng (attested 2013).

Minonori Nishimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Taisho University (~1971–1976) studying under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, served on its faculty (~1993–2018), and was a researcher at Sanko Research Institute (attested 2002).

Minoru Hara was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1981, attested 1989–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2006), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2004–2012).

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1946–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1954–1963) under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa. He was a long-time professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–2013).
Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1866–1870). He served on the faculty at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1899) and Harvard University (~1899–1907).

Miranda Shaw is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied with doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1994) and Robert A. F. Thurman, and completed postdoctoral work under B. N. Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, later holding professorships at the University of Bucharest (~1933–1938), University of Paris (attested 1965), and University of Chicago (~1956–1986).
Mireille Helffer was a tibetologist who held posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique as Chargé de Recherche (~1961–1993) and at Paris Nanterre University (~1967–1989).

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD from the University of Calgary under John A. Baker (-2005), and held posts at the University of New South Wales and University of Western Australia (attested 2006).

Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).
Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Ljubljana (~1955–1960) and served on the faculty at Yale Law School (~1976–2023).

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942). He held academic posts at the University of Kitakyushu (~1953–1961), the University of Tokyo (~1961–1970), Kyoto University (~1970–1982), and Kansai University (~1982–1989).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and held an affiliation at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saigusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950), he taught at Kokugakuin University and was a professor and professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba (~1974–2010).

Mitsuyuki Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1932–1935). He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1952–1979) and later at Shitennoji University (attested 1976).

Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University and Gakushuin University under Katsuhiko Kamimura and doctoral supervisor Atsuhiko Yoshida, and served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University (attested 2008).
